title: The humans pray in a sail-loft at Cuan shean
summary: On the day the strangers keep for their god a sailmaker of Cuan shean lends them his loft against the rain. They kneel on the sailcloth, the captain with the rest, while a priest reads from a book; they light no fire and burn nothing. Two priests of Manannan watch from the stair and go down to the water to say their own prayer. It is the first entry of the humans at prayer under a roof.

title: Crìosd and an Eaglais written in the council roll
summary: In the same season as an Tìr Thall the clerk of Comhairle a' Chùraim enters the name of the strangers' one god as the island hears it, Crìosd, and calls their faith an Eaglais, after the word their priests use of the whole company of their believers. They are the first words of the humans' tongue that the island takes and keeps.

title: The keeping of the word-list given to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair
summary: The humans' priests ask Cuan shean for someone to trade words with them at a table, and Cuan shean sends to the capital. Tormod mac Ailein calls Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, who sits on the council for Clann Fhearchair and writes the best hand in the hall, and the council gives her the keeping of the island's side of the list. Her niece Muireall is to make the fair copy.

title: Wren and the priests come up to Cathair dhearg
summary: Two priests of the humans and a boy ride up from Cuan shean on ponies of the town, a long day's road, and come over the bridge at dusk soaked through. The council lodges them in a house below the temple and gives them a long room on the east side of the hall. The younger priest, Samuel Wren, coughs in the damp of the lake country.

title: Wren sets his months against the moons
summary: Wren draws the twelve months of the humans' sun-year as a wheel, and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives him the island's moons from Samhnas round to the stags' moon. He writes each moon's name beside the month it most nearly matches. For Eadrach, the between-moon, he finds no place, and writes it outside the wheel with the humans' mark of a question.

title: Wren names the fuel of his own country
summary: Over a brazier of peat in the long room Wren shows by signs that his people burn peat too, and also a black stone dug from under the ground, which they burn in every house. Gormshuil nic Fhearchair writes his word for it and, in the Dia-thìris column, the black stone the humans dig in their own country and burn on their hearths.

title: The basket of broken coal on the table
summary: In the wolf-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair takes a double handful from the capital's measure for the shrines and tips it on the table before Samuel Wren in the winter sun. She names forty colours at the breaks. Wren writes some of them, then stops, turns a piece in the light and gives one word for the whole heap. She waits for him to ask for hers; he holds up a candle.

title: Muireall copies the first leaf
summary: In the gap-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives her loose sheets to her niece Muireall to copy fair into a book for Clann Fhearchair, and orders the colours set first, before cup and bread, alone on the first leaf with room left at the foot. Muireall copies the forty words in her young, careful hand and stops at the right-hand column, where the humans' side has one word to give.

title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair begins the humans' letters
summary: Since Wren cannot learn her colours, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks him by signs to teach her his letters. He writes them across a sheet of his white paper, large and small, and her name beneath as he hears it, and she copies it stroke by stroke. By the end of the spring she can spell out a line of his word-list, and finds his one word under her colours.

title: The first bargains entered in the council roll
summary: At the moon of the bright fire the strangers' iron, glass, lamp-oil and paper come up to the capital's market, and wool, hides, salt fish and dyed cloth go down to Cuan shean. Comhairle a' Chùraim enters the first bargains in its roll, fleece for knife and cloth for glass, with both prices in the island's reckoning. The measure is good on both sides.

title: The copy of the list sent to the loft at Muileann chaol
summary: Having watched the humans burn their spoiled paper, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair has Muireall make a second fair copy of the whole list, the colours first and the note at the foot of the first leaf. She seals it in an oak chest with the seal of Clann Fhearchair and sends it east with the carriers to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais, where nothing is burned.
